title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - trivia 
 trivia : Due to what was observed from Artorias, the phrase "falling into the Abyss" does not actually constitute entering it, but rather the near infinite and unconscious darkness of it seeking out lifeforms.
**This likely means that Wolnir was very much alive when he fell, which explains how he was able to teach grave wardens his pyromancy, though what exactly it really was that actually caused his death is uncertain.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : The Abyss is a realm of Dark born from the Dark Soul or its fragments. It's an ecosystem capable of creating life, as generated by one of the core components of the First Flame, and of expanding while slowly absorbing everything in its path; it is uninhabitable to all beings aligned with Fire including the Gods, as they require special equipment or protection to prevent corruption (both in the spiritual and physical sense). In contrast, any beings aligned with or indifferent to the Abyss (such as Humans) are able to roam it with no risk of harm or corruption.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - location 
 location : In Dark Souls the Abyss is located at the end of the New Londo Ruins. To reach to the Abyss, the floodgates must be lowered and the Covenant of Artorias ring, a reward for killing Great Grey Wolf Sif, must be worn. After climbing down a spiral staircase within a tower, the path will abruptly end, making it necessary to descend into the darkness of the Abyss.

The DLC *Artorias of the Abyss* allows us to explore a more recent Abyss, despite being located in a past era, deep within the dungeons of Oolacile.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : It is possible to reach and kill the Four Kings by killing Ingward, even if the player hasn't acquired the Lordvessel yet.
The bonfire that appears *will* allow warping to escape the Abyss, even without the Lordvessel.
**This can be used as a shortcut for far away locations, such as Anor Londo, Tomb of the Giants or Ash Lake. If the player avoids resting at other bonfires, the Abyss can be used as a "home base", warping to locations in Lordran, and returning via Homeward Bone.
Although it appears to be a black void of nothingness, the "ground" of the abyss actually floats a few meters above an unseen cobblestone floor. This can be observed by using a light source, such as the Skull Lantern or Sunlight Maggot.
Items that require hitting a surface to activate, such as Prism Stones and Carvings, will not work in the Abyss as they simply fall through the "floor".

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The **Abyss** is a location in *Dark Souls*, as well as a storyline concept featured in all three games in the series.

The in-game location is at the heart of the New Londo Ruins, a featureless expanse where the Chosen Undead must slay the Four Kings and can encounter Darkstalker Kaathe. As a concept, "Abyss" is the name given to both a force that consumes or corrupts most forms of life, and to the areas in which it dwells; it is tied to the Age of Dark, and also gave birth to a twisted offshoot known as The Deep.

title: Abyss
snippet: Knight Artorias famously traversed New Londo's Abyss and hunted the Darkwraiths therein. He was protected by the power of a magical ring, which he gained after making a covenant with the beasts there. The ring prevented him from being swallowed by the void, but it led to his sword becoming cursed. In recognition of his actions, he was awarded one of Anor Londo's treasures, a Silver Pendant that allowed him to repel Dark sorceries; eventually he traveled to Oolacile to combat the threat of Manus, the lord of the Abyss. He ultimately failed in his mission he was overtaken by the dark, leaving behind his companion Sif.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Anastacia strongly resembles the Maiden in Black from *Demon's Souls*: the maiden is an ally to the Slayer of Demons like Anastacia is an ally to the Chosen Undead. Both of them have some physical impairment: the Maiden is blind, and Anastacia is mute. They are also both guardians to sacred places.
It appears that Anastacia is locked in her cell in Firelink Shrine; however, in the prologue, she is seen kneeling over an unnamed undead in the graveyard.
The description of the Blood-Stained Skirt implies that, as well as having her tongue cut out, Anastacia's legs were crippled to keep her from leaving Firelink Shrine. Her model is missing both legs around the knees.
Her name translates from Greek ἀνάστασις as “revived” that closely links to her fate.

title: Anastacia of Astora

 location : She can be found in a cell below the Firelink Shrine bonfire, down the stairs located to the left of the Crestfallen Warrior.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Initially, she is unable to speak, for her tongue has been removed sometime ago. Nonetheless, the player can still interact with her. As with other Fire Keepers, Anastacia has the ability to reinforce the Estus Flask, in exchange for Fire Keeper Souls.

If Knight Lautrec of Carim is in Firelink Shrine, he will kill Anastacia when either of the following occurs:

The player rings both Bells of Awakening.
The player picks up the Fire Keeper Souls in the Undead Parish and in Blighttown.

While Anastacia is dead the bonfire in Firelink Shrine is inactive and unusable. She leaves behind the Dingy Set and the Black Eye Orb. The Black Eye Orb is an invasion item, allowing players to find and invade Lautrec's world to defeat him and retrieve Anastacia's Fire Keeper Soul.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Anastacia of Astora** (アストラのアナスタシア), also known as **The Ash Maiden,** is a Fire Keeper in *Dark Souls*. She keeps the bonfire in Firelink Shrine lit.

Anastacia is voiced by Emma Pierson, who also voiced Dusk of Oolacile.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Anastacia of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Anastacia is suggested by herself and at least one other character to be "impure", mainly of speech. However, what exactly made her "unclean" is never revealed, as she tells very little to the player even with her tongue restored. It has been hinted from item descriptions that Anastacia may have chosen her own banishment and even imprisonment.

title: Anastacia of Astora
snippet:
Returning Anastacia's soul to her cage will revive her, reigniting the Firelink Shrine bonfire. Her speech will also be restored, allowing the player to engage in conversation with her.

Once Anastacia is revived, if the player places the Lordvessel, offers at least one Lord Soul or Lord Soul Shard to it, and then talks to her, she will fully kindle the Firelink Shrine bonfire.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Besides hailing from Astora, little is known about Andre; he seems to cherish dependability, which might vaguely suggest a history of betrayal, though this is never elaborated upon. He is also acquainted with the Giant Blacksmith, as evidenced when he notices the player holding the Giant's Coal.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Andre's stocky build, beard, dour demeanor and profession as a blacksmith of legendary weapons resembles popular depictions of the *dwarves*, originally of Norse myth, and later popularized by the works of Tolkien and *Dungeons & Dragons*.
**Andre's name is similar to that of the dwarf *Andvari* of Norse myth.
**Bodies of blacksmiths closely resembling Andre are found in various locations, seemingly petrified. In Norse myth, dwarves are said to be turned to stone by sunlight. Two of the petrified dwarves in Dark Souls are located in ruined buildings which appear to have been exposed to sunlight due to structural damage.
**Dwarves in Norse myth are famed for the creation of magic items, particularly magic weapons of unparalleled strength. These include Thor's hammer *Mjolnir*, Odin's spear *Gungnir*, the reforged sword *Gram*, and the cursed sword *Tyrfing*.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Andre of Astora is located directly below the bonfire in the Undead Parish, between Darkroot Garden and Sen's Fortress.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Often the first blacksmith new players come across, Andre of Astora can be a welcome sight. Andre of Astora is the only blacksmith that can ascend weapons down the Standard path from +5 to +6 and from +10 to +11. He is also the only blacksmith that can ascend weapons down the Raw, Divine and Occult paths.

He also sells some basic upgrade materials, as well as many weapons (some of which are unique to him). Finally, he sells the Crest of Artorias, which is required to open the door to Darkroot Forest, a more dangerous section of Darkroot Garden.

In *Dark Souls III*, he acts as the blacksmith in Firelink Shrine. At the beginning he is unable to infuse weapons without the correspondent coals found through the game to expand his services. Once the player has found a coal, returning it to him will unlock new infusion options.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre has a west country accent, a region in the UK famous as the supposed birthplace of King Arthur. While it's likely a choice of actor, the fact remains he is one of the few with a true regional English accent. Notably, the west country is frequently depicted/stereotyped as the countryside in media. The line by Rickert, "an old smith out in the country", may allude to Andre.
Andre is one of the few characters that do not disintegrate when killed. This may be because he uses a unique model, or perhaps signifies he is not an Undead or monster.
It was originally intended that Andre was to be a descendant of Gwyn and that he would have a key role in the story, but this idea was scrapped.
Andre is one of the few characters in *Dark Souls* whose mouth moves when he speaks (the others being Quelaag's Sister, Kingseeker Frampt, Alvina and Darkstalker Kaathe).

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Andre of Astora** (アストラのアンドレイ) is a character in *Dark Souls*. He is a blacksmith that will likely prove invaluable to the player throughout the game. Andre is voiced by Sean Barrett, who also voiced Ingward and Petrus of Thorolund.

title: Andre of Astora
snippet:
Andre of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Despite what common sense might dictate, Andre does not use his hammer to fight, preferring to simply use his bare hands. This certainly does not mean that he is a pushover, however; his heavier punches can knock players off their feet, while his jabs are fast and can quickly deal a lot of damage. Andre has a roster of moves unique to him, including a drop kick that has heavy knockback and deals high damage. He also sports unusually high health for a character of his stature, so it may take a while to wear him down.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Balder Knights came to Lordran in large numbers along with their king, Knight King Rendal, seeking a cure for the Undead curse. However, none were able to defeat the Iron Golem, and they ended up as Hollows in the Undead Parish or Sen's Fortress.

It is possible that at least one Balder Knight managed to enter Anor Londo, becoming a member of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - general_information 
 general_information : There are three varieties of Balder Knights: Side Sword, Rapier, and Crossbow. Those wielding rapiers are stronger and drop more souls.

The Rapier variant of the Balder Knight can switch stances, holding its weapon at chest level, pointed at the player. While its stance is altered thus, the Balder Knight can parry.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Several corpses of Balder knights can be found in the Undead Parish and Sen's Fortress, and are the only preplaced corpses in the game to have armor on their dead body.
Their armor has a similar design to the armor worn by Guts, the protagonist of the *Berserk* anime/manga, during its Golden Age arc.

title: Balder Knight
snippet:
Balder Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Balder Knights have a fair amount of health, and are a considerable threat to new characters. Even one-on-one, they can be very dangerous.

Any ranged attack is useful against them, but they are fast and will close the gap quickly. Firebombs can be very useful in defeating them.

Critical attacks, such as the Parry and Riposte and Backstab, are exceedingly efficient methods to dispatch these enemies.

title: Banshee
snippet: If possible, the most complete strategy is to use a Transient Curse, but still wield a cursed weapon. This makes it so that the player is not left completely defenseless should the Transient Curse end at a bad time, or without the player noticing.

title: Banshee
snippet:
Banshee -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : They scream when the player gets too close, and is said to attract other ghosts. The main differences between Banshees and Ghosts are their red, glowing eyes, the Ghost Blade half-held in one hand, and the baby they carry.

title: Banshee
snippet:
Banshee -  Dark Souls - enemy - curse 
 curse : Like the Ghost, the Banshee can only be killed if the player is Cursed, or is carrying a cursed weapon. Transient Curse allows temporary contact with a Banshee without actually being cursed. This is considered a self augmentation effect, and thus prevents the use of other self augmentations.

If the player is not cursed, they will not be able to interact with the Banshee in any way. This includes damaging it, of course, but also blocking it, or just reducing the damage taken with armor. Furthermore, the Banshee's attacks will always stagger the player when not cursed, as it bypasses armor, leaving the player poiseless.

Players can also use cursed weapons (such as the Jagged Ghost Blade or the Cursed Greatsword of Artorias). While this allows striking the Banshee, it will still leave the player unable to block with a shield, or reduce damage taken with armor. Cursed weapons can also be held with two hands to block.

 trivia : The Bell Gargoyles boss fight is based on the Maneaters boss fight from *Demon's Souls*.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : Gargoyles are stone creatures created by the Gods through magic to help patrol Anor Londo or sites deemed important. In addition to their tough and hard skin, they are able to breathe fire or lightning and are armed with a bronze shield and a bronze helmet for purely decorative purposes while they use a bronze halberd as a weapon.

After Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the First Flame and prolong the Age of Fire, several Gargoyles were placed to guard the Bell of Awakening placed on the Undead Church of the Undead Burg and act as ritual challenge. The Undead who wished to follow in Gwyn's footsteps to sacrifice themselves to the Flame would have to be tested before obtaining the Lordvessel and seeking powerful souls. Ringing the Bells of Awakening represents only the first of these challenges, and success means gaining access to Sen's Fortress to be tested further.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - anor_londo_mini_bosses 
 anor_londo_mini_bosses : The two Gargoyles fought in Anor Londo breathe lightning rather than fire, so a lightning-resistant shield will prove beneficial. A strategy for the second gargoyle is for the player to run to the bottom of the rotating staircase before activating the lever, where the gargoyle (on a ledge above) will be unable to reach them. However, this means it must then be defeated with ranged attacks.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Bell Gargoyles** (鐘のガーゴイル) are dual bosses in *Dark Souls*.

There are four Gargoyles in the game: the first two are part of the same boss battle atop the Undead Parish, with the second only joining halfway through, while the last two are mini-bosses found in Anor Londo. None of them respawn.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - description 
 description : They appear to be armored gargoyles wielding axes and shields with fire or lightning attacks. They have axes on their tails which they use to swing at you.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : In human form, it is possible to have Solaire of Astora and/or Knight Lautrec of Carim assist during this battle, although Lautrec must be freed and spoken to in Firelink Shrine first. Their summon signs are found just before the white light leading to the Gargoyles. Summoning both knights and simply mobbing each Gargoyle can lead to a quick and relatively painless victory.

The fight is beset by the constant danger of falling off (target-locking, coupled with the camera angle and narrow field of view, can make it hard to track the player character's footing) and facing off against a single gargoyle on top of the church roof. Trying to circle the gargoyle while holding up a shield is a good way to avoid its long-reaching frontal attacks. If the gargoyle takes off, move away or get ready to dodge its plunging attack.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - location 
 location : On top of the church in the Undead Parish, reached by passing through the room full of hollows and a Channeler, before climbing two ladders and finally entering the fog gate. They are also found in Anor Londo as mini-bosses: Exit the first bonfire, go straight on and down the lift, and a gargoyle will be straight ahead. The second is beyond the rotating staircase-bridge.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Once the first gargoyle is cut down to half its health, the second gargoyle will join the fight. Fortunately, this gargoyle is already severely injured (it arrives at half-health). It has the same attacks as the first gargoyle minus those that involve flying or using the tail.

Players having difficulty managing their positioning against the two gargoyles should save any consumables (ex., Fire Bombs) until the first gargoyle's health is approaching 50%, and then use them to finish it off as quickly as possible. For as long as both gargoyles are alive, players should keep them both on the screen; if not feasible, one can try following audio cues to perceive an oncoming attack. The use of Gold Pine Resin and other weapon enhancements can greatly help in finishing off the first gargoyle, and make the overall fight significantly easier.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Both Gargoyles wield halberds and can breathe fire, although the first gargoyle usually will only breathe fire after the second one jumps down. A fire-resistant shield such as the Black Knight Shield (and, optionally, fire-resistant armor) can be very useful, as the fire breath covers a wide area. While breathing fire, the gargoyles won't move, making it the perfect opportunity to run over and hit them from behind (this makes avoiding or blocking the fire twice as important, as its stagger effect will consume precious seconds, limiting the time available to attack the gargoyles).

The first gargoyle's tail can be severed to gain a weapon (Gargoyle Tail Axe).

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The Bells of Awakening are hinted at being the first destination of the Chosen Undead and, when rung, the fate of the undead shall be known. Upon arriving in Firelink Shrine, the Crestfallen Warrior informs the player that there are, in fact, two Bells of Awakening. One up above and one far below. This is essentially all the instruction and plot that is revealed upon arrival in Lordran.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Ringing the bell in Quelaag's Domain first will have no different effect than if the player rang the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] first. Although this will cause Lautrec's questline to progress, leading to the death of Anastacia.
The Bells of Awakening were used to awaken Kingseeker Frampt and open the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - undead_church_bell 
 undead_church_bell : One of the Bells is located in the Undead Parish, up above from Firelink Shrine. After dispatching the Bell Gargoyles, the Chosen Undead is able to climb to the top of the Church Belltower and ring the Bell of Awakening.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : In the Prepare to Die Edition, online players in the vicinity of the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] were able to hear the bell being rung from other player worlds. This wasn’t the case for the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Bell in Quelaag’s Domain].
In the remastered version of the game, online players are now able to hear either the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] or the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s domain Bell] being rung from other player worlds while exploring one area or the other . (as the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s Bell] toll was specifically added in the remaster)

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Berenike Knights were known for their heavy armor of steel and their ultra-heavy Tower Shields forged with thick plates of iron, favoring hard defense and stability, as well as their gigantic swords capable of causing enormous damage. For their immense strength these knights were extolled as the mightiest of mighty. Among them, Black Iron Tarkus was renowned even among his fellow knights for his great strength; he wore an ultra-heavy armor made of special black iron—one with exceptional fire protection, yet so unwieldy that only he was able to wear it; his greatshield, made of the same fire-resistant material, was even heavier than that of his fellow knights.

snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Large and clad in the Steel Set, they wield either a large Mace or Greatsword, depending on the location where they are found, along with a Tower Shield. All Berenike Knights can be parried, but cannot be riposted.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, probably accompanied by some fellow knights, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - location 
 location : Undead Parish — A Berenike Knight Demon can be found near the Undead Church as a miniboss guarding the Fire Keeper Soul.
Sen's Fortress — Berenike Knights can be found as respawning enemies.
Painted World of Ariamis — Berenike Knights can be found as respawning enemies.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : is a character in *Dark Souls*. First met in Sen's Fortress, from which he relocates to Firelink Shrine, he is a merchant of advanced sorceries, including new ones upon following his questline into The Duke's Archives.

Voiced by Ian Thompson in his final role before his passing in 2022, Logan is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II* and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*, although *Dark Souls II* refers to him as an unnamed "master sorcerer" due to his name being forgotten in Drangleic.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Master Logan was a famous Sorcerer and a royal member of the Vinheim Dragon School before he turned Undead about one hundred years ago. His nickname stems from the gigantic hat he wore which completely hid his face; he used it to block the noise and stares from those around him in order to focus his thoughts. His weapon was once an ordinary catalyst employed by the Sorcerers of Vinheim, but it has since been strengthened due to lengthy use over time. His sage robe, called prototype, meaning it goes back the School foundation of the Dragon School, therefore the School was founded around the times Logan was alive.

Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Big Hat Logan seems to prefer sitting down in a meditative position, except for the first encounter when he's in a hanging jail cage.
If you get the Man-Serpent leaning against the wall next to the cage he is in, It will break, meaning you don't need to get the boulder trap to break it, with careful planning.
Logan shares many similarities with Sage Freke from *Demon's Souls*. Both are first found trapped in cages and rescued by the player. Both are preceded by apprentices looking for them, have an unhealthy fascination with magic, and are found sitting in the main hub area.
Rickert of Vinheim mentions to the player that Big Hat Logan is famous in Vinheim; however, he also mentions that Logan was from "a hundred years ago". Either Logan has remained sane for as long as he has been undead, or time warping in Lordran has brought Logan to a time where one does not belong.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
When Logan is encountered hostile, he is not hollowed, but was driven insane in a more "traditional" sense. All other NPCs appear in their charred, undead forms when they attack players after hollowing.
If the player dies fighting against Big Hat Logan while in Seath's arena, the player will respawn in the prison as if they were killed by Seath himself, which underlines that Logan became just as mad as Seath.
Logan's Tin Crystallization Catalyst is actually 結晶の錫杖 ("Crystall Staff"). 錫杖 (khakkhara), is a ringed staff used by Buddhist monks. This implies that Logan venerated Seath as a God.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Big Hat Logan is first encountered in Sen's Fortress. His cage is hidden behind a wall, which can be destroyed by manipulating the iron ball trap mechanism, using a powerful enough weapon, or goading the sleeping man-serpent guard to attack the wall. After freeing him with either the Cage Key or Master Key, Big Hat Logan thanks the player and later retreats to Firelink Shrine. There, he accompanies Griggs of Vinheim and offers to sell the player advanced Sorceries.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

He is also the creator of Homing Soulmass, a sinister spell similar to Pursuers and therefore closer to dark sorceries, which enlights a more shady side of Logan. Griggs affirms that Logan has not concern for others, and that he is an unreasonable and troublesome man.

In his attempt to reach Anor Londo, presumably to gain access to The Duke's Archives and its vast store of endless knowledge, he became imprisoned in Sen's Fortress, where he first encounters the Chosen Undead.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:

Only available at The Duke's Archives

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : Big Hat's Set and Logan's Catalyst are found in a chest where he normally sits in The Duke's Archives after he goes insane and travels to the arena where Seath is first encountered. (The elevator is likely at the top of its shaft and the lever will need to be used to bring it back. It is recessed and hidden on the first floor.) The player must kill Logan then trigger a loading screen (either by logging out or using a Homeward Bone) to make the chest appear.
When Big Hat Logan is battled, he wears no clothes except for his big hat, because he has gone insane.
When spoken to in the Duke's Archives there is no Intelligence requirement to purchase his spells.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan soon leaves Firelink Shrine after the Lordvessel has been obtained. He is then jailed in The Duke's Archives. Logan explains that he is there to study Seath the Scaleless and his magic. After freeing him with the Archive Tower Giant Cell Key, players can find Logan in an ancillary library close to the third bonfire in The Duke's Archives, where he sells Crystal Sorceries as well as his prior spells. Alternatively, if not freed by you by Seath's defeat, he will free himself and move to the library.

Unfortunately, Logan's infatuation with Seath's magic eventually drives him insane after Seath has been defeated and his entire stock of spells has been purchased. Speaking with him again, after the above conditions are met, will cause him to move to the large chamber where Seath the Scaleless was first encountered and become hostile.

title: Estus Flask (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Estus Flask (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - item - effect 
 effect : Estus Flasks are the basic healing items in *Dark Souls*. They are replenished via resting at bonfires. The amount they heal can be upgraded by offering Fire Keeper Souls to other Fire Keepers. The maximum amount of times an Estus flask can be upgraded is seven times. Only seven fire keeper souls can be obtained in one game. Four of these can be found scattered throughout the world, but the other three must be obtained by killing the firekeepers to claim their souls (or in the case of Anastacia of Astora, obtaining her soul from Lautrec after he kills her).

title: Estus Flask (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Estus Flask (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - item - notes 
 notes : Firekeeper souls are very rare (only 7 can be found per playthrough, and three are held by NPCs that the player may not want to kill or let die) and, though they can be consumed for humanity, they are usually better spent upgrading estus flasks. Upgrading estus flasks dramatically improves the player's ability to heal him or herself. For example, a player with twenty +7 Estus Flasks can heal up to 10,000 more HP in total than a player with twenty non-upgraded Flasks.

Phantoms of all types cannot rely on estus flasks for healing. However, they can still rely on all other healing items and spells, such as the Heal miracle, consuming solid humanity, etc. Friendly phantoms (not including NPC) are healed by estus whenever their host player uses one.

Players hit by a Lloyd's Talisman will not be able to drink estus for a limited duration.

title: Sublime Bone Dust
snippet:
Sublime Bone Dust -  Dark Souls II - item - usage 
 usage : Burning it at the Far Fire bonfire in Majula results in a bolstering of the player's Estus Flask (similar to the role of Fire Keeper Souls in the original *Dark Souls*). This can be done until the player's Estus Flask is +5; a +5 Flask being the most potent in terms of health restoration.

They can still be collected even after the Flask is upgraded to +5, but their only practical use is to be sold to Lonesome Gavlan for 1,800 souls each.

An emerald flask, from the Keeper's soul

 And dies to protect it further.

title: Estus Flask (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Estus Flask (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - overview 
 overview : The player starts with three Estus Flask charges at the beginning of the game. In addition, the Ashen Estus Flask can be picked up a short distance into the tutorial area, granting an overall total of four charges. Drinking from the flask restores HP (the Ashen Estus Flask restores FP). Resting at a bonfire will refill all Estus Flasks to maximum charges.

To increase the number of Estus Flask charges, the player must first find an Estus Shard and bring it to Blacksmith Andre in Firelink Shrine, where they will also be able to allot the total number of uses between the standard and the ashen Estus Flasks. The combined total between both Estus Flasks can reach a maximum of 15 charges. Any additional Estus Shards obtained afterward will have no practical use, since they cannot be sold.

title: Estus Flask (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Estus Flask (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - item - availability

Additional Estus Flasks may be obtained with each Estus Flask Shard brought to her, up to a limit of 12.
Sublime Bone Dust can be found in the game, which increases the amount of health an Estus Flask heals by 50 HP each, to a maximum of +5.

All that is known now is that this flask remains a prized possession of the Undead.

title: Estus Flask (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Estus Flask (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : An Estus flask is first granted to the player by Oscar before he succumbs to death. Alternately, the player automatically receives the Estus Flask if they kill Oscar. Thereafter, players receive up to 5 Estus charges by resting at an unkindled bonfire. A kindled bonfire yields 10 charges; further kindling bonfires through Rite of Kindling rewards an additional 5 charges per kindle to up to 20 in total. Additionally, if the bonfire last rested at is kindled by another player, the player receives an extra Estus charge, unless the player is at 20 Estus, which is the maximum amount possible.

snippet:

 notes : Summoned shades cannot drink Estus during most PvP. Only hosts or Dragon Eye users can use the Estus Flask during PvP, where the host heals friendly shades.

title: Estus Flask (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Estus Flask (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - item - general_information 
 general_information : Estus Flasks restore life more quickly than Lifegems, but initially come in a much more limited quantity. Unlike Lifegems, Estus Flasks are automatically refilled at bonfires.
A +0 Estus Flask heals for 550, and a +5 Estus Flask heals for 800.
Drinking an Estus Flask stops the player completely. With this in mind, it might be beneficial to use a Lifegem if the player is in a pinch, as they only slow down movement speed while used.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
Fire Keeper -  Dark Souls III - character - general_information 
 general_information : In *Dark Souls*, bonfires watched over by Fire Keepers are automatically kindled to provide ten Estus Flask charges each. Still they may be upgraded through the Rite of Kindling, just like other bonfires. All Fire Keepers have special souls and drop a Fire Keeper Soul upon death. Fire Keepers universally share the ability to upgrade Estus Flasks using the souls of their fellow Fire Keepers. The death or departure of a Fire Keeper will lead to the bonfire they attended to be extinguished, and it can no longer be used to rest, level up or teleport from using the Lordvessel. The description of the regular Fire Keeper Soul states that "Each Fire Keeper is a corporeal manifestation of her bonfire, and a draw for the humanity which is offered to her."

title: Ashen Estus Flask
snippet:
Ashen Estus Flask -  Dark Souls III - item - overview 
 overview : Drinking from the Ashen Estus Flask restores FP, much like how the normal Estus Flask restores HP. Resting at a bonfire will refill it to maximum charges.

The total number of shared charges between the normal Estus Flask and Ashen Estus Flask can be increased by bringing Estus Shards to Blacksmith Andre, and the potency of each charge increased by burning an Undead Bone Shard at Firelink Shrine's bonfire. The number of total charges between the two flasks can reach a maximum of 15, while the potency of the flasks can reach a maximum of +10. The player can also talk to Blacksmith Andre to allot their Estus charges between the two flasks.

The potency of each charge of the Ashen Estus Flask can be increased by 20% by equipping the Ashen Estus Ring.

These containers will refill each time an area is loaded, so if the player has already depleted one and does not want to rest at a bonfire in order to avoid repopulating the area, all they have to do is exit and continue the game, and the pot will be replenished with a new dose. title: Fire Keeper Soul
snippet:
Fire Keeper Soul -  Dark Souls - item - notes 
 notes : The player may not have duplicates of a Fire Keeper's unique soul (obtained by killing an in-game Fire Keeper), meaning only seven can be carried at a time. Thus, it's good to make a habit of offering them to Fire Keepers whenever one finds them until the Estus Flask is fully reinforced.
The Estus Flask can only be reinforced a total of 7 times, meaning that only 7 Fire Keeper's souls may be used in such a manner. Any subsequent souls obtained (only possible past NG as each playthrough yields a maximum of 7) may as well be consumed.
Anastacia's Fire Keeper Soul can be used to revive her, allowing the player to re-access the Firelink Shrine bonfire and speak to her. If her soul is used instead, the fire can never be re-lit until the next playthrough.
As it requires an active Fire Keeper to reinforce the player's Estus Flask, it is not possible to obtain +7 Flasks on one playthrough.

She gives the player an Estus Flask upon introducing herself. Bringing her Estus Flask Shards will increase the total amount of charges that the Flask can hold.

She gives the player the Aged Feather when spoken to upon arrival in Dragon Aerie.

title: Nehma, Goddess of Love
snippet:
Nehma, Goddess of Love -  Dark Souls II - character - theories 
 theories : It's possible that Nehma is connected to the Goddess Fina, maybe even being the name she was given by the people of Drangleic and its neighbors. While her domain is not fully established, love seems to be quite a big part of Fina's character, even if fickle by nature.

Another possible connection to Fina is through the Estus Flask, the symbol of Nehma. In *Dark Souls*, Estus Flasks were enhanched using Fire Keeper Souls, and Knigh Lautrec's mission involved killing the Fire Keeper in Firelink Shrine and presumably taking her soul to his goddess.

title: Blacksmith Andre
snippet:
In addition to upgrading and infusing weapons, Andre can repair those that are broken. He cannot repair the Ring of Sacrifice, though.

Andre allows the player character to allocate between a standard Estus Flask and the Ashen Estus Flask. For example, if the player has five Estus Flask uses in total, they can choose to have three standard Estus Flasks uses, which recover HP, and two Ashen Estus Flask uses, which recover FP.

Finally, Andre can reinforce the player's Estus Flask to increase its number of uses. In order for Andre to upgrade the Estus Flask, the player must bring him an Estus Shard.

If the player kills Andre, he will no longer offer any services, unless the player's sins are forgiven at the shrine of Velka.

title: Oscar, Knight of Astora
snippet:
Oscar is reminiscent of Ostrava of Boletaria from *Demon's Souls*, as they both wear signature armors from their respective games, use powerful weapons imbued with magic, and turn hostile to the player after their deaths.
Oscar and the Black Knights in the Asylum can damage each other, although they will never attack each other intentionally.
In *Dark Souls III*, a corpse wearing the Elite Knight Set is found in the Cemetery of Ash, sitting in a pose reminiscent of Oscar. This corpse can be looted to obtain the first Ashen Estus Flask of the game, likely in reference to how Oscar gave the player the Estus Flask in the first game.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
In *Dark Souls II*, the three Fire Keepers in Things Betwixt and the Emerald Herald, believed by some to be Fire Keeper, can be killed without the nearby bonfire being affected. The way the Herald can level up the Bearer of the Curse is reminescent of how the Fire Keepers in *Dark Souls III* can the Ashen One. One of the Keepers, Strowen, offers the player to re-allocate their attributes in exchange for a Soul Vessel.

In *Dark Souls III*, the unnamed Fire Keeper can level up the Ashen One like the Hemerald did in the previous game. She is also immortal; killing her, in addition to not causing the Shrine bonfire to be affected, will only cause her to respawn upon reloading the area, claiming that she cannot die. Instead of a Keeper, it is Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth, the leader of the Rosaria's Fingers covenant, who allows the player to re-allocate their attributes.

title: Divine Blessing
snippet:
Divine Blessing -  Dark Souls - item - overview 
 overview : Divine Blessings are some of the best healing items in the game. They heal more quickly than using the Estus Flask, making them superior to using Humanity and the healing miracles in terms of speed. They also cannot be blocked by Lloyd's Talismans, unlike Estus. In addition, they can be used while invading.

However, they can only be obtained in very limited quantities, so it is wise to only use them in times of dire emergency.

title: Hollowing
snippet:
Hollowing -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - healing_the_dark_sigil 
 healing_the_dark_sigil : The more permanent option for curing Hollowing is to obtain the Fire Keeper Soul and give it to the Fire Keeper. The player must then pay a soul cost equal to the amount of souls they would pay to level up from their current level, by a number of levels equal to the amount of Dark Sigils held. Thus, if the player is high level and has accepted the additional Dark Sigils from Anri of Astora's wedding, the price for healing the Dark Sigil can be extremely high.

Healing the Dark Sigil is permanent, as it will remove all held Dark Sigils and reset Hollowing to zero. Because of this, it will break the alliance with Yuria of Londor, as the Dark Sigils are required for obtaining the Usurpation of Fire ending.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet: All confirmed Fire Keepers in the series, as well as prospective Fire Keeper Irina of Carim and the possible Fire Keepers that are the Emerald Herald and mentionned fourth sister in *Dark Souls II*, are female, as are seemingly all of the dead Fire Keepers whose bodies can be found in the Firelink Shrine of *Dark Souls III*. The description of the generic Fire Keeper Soul in *Dark Souls* similarly refers to "Each Fire Keeper" using female pronouns. Whether the reason is cultural or biological is unclear.

snippet:
Kiln of the First Flame (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The new version of the familiar place is where lies the First Flame and its guardian, the Soul of Cinder. The location has been greatly altered since its depiction in *Dark Souls*.

Once the player has gathered all of the Lords of Cinder, the Fire Keeper will perform a ritual in which the flames of the Lords will drift to her hands. She will then scatter the flames onto the player, teleporting them to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Darkmoon Knightess
snippet:
Darkmoon Knightess -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : The Darkmoon Knightess is one of Dark Sun Gwyndolin's loyal followers and the fire keeper of the first bonfire in Anor Londo. As with the other fire keepers, the Darkmoon Knightess can upgrade Estus Flasks using Fire Keeper Souls. Like all other fire keepers, killing the Darkmoon Knightess will cause the fire she watches over to be extinguished, although players can still warp to it after obtaining the Lordvessel.

Should the player kill Gwynevere, the Darkmoon Knightess will appear directly in front of the elevator of Anor Londo to offer punishment for the deed. Should the player attack Dark Sun Gwyndolin, the Darkmoon Knightess will also become hostile and reside in her usual location, the first Anor Londo bonfire. Her armor, the Brass Set can be found in the room with the sunlight blade miracle after defeating Dark Sun Gwyndolin.

This Fire Keeper preserves the bonfire, and serves its champion. She is said to have soothed and accepted the dark sigil, which has tainted her soul.

And yet, her soul will one day embed itself in the bosom of another Fire Keeper.
